analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Fed Sparks Bull Steepening As ECB Looms And Gilts Absorb Budget
key_insights: The Fed statement read as hawkish to the author, including Governor Cook's dissent, but the market treated the change to the 2027 and 2028 meeting schedule as dovish, inferring fewer live meetings and fewer hikes. The author thinks that inference is wrong.
SFRZ7 rallied more than 10 ticks from Wednesday's low of 95.34, which suggests the market agrees with the dovish reading of the meeting-schedule change.

Chair Warsh said in the press conference that the economy was not running too hot and that financial conditions were tighter. Markets now price 20.6bp of hikes in December, and some Street commentators suggest December could be the last hike of the cycle.

UBS US chief economist Jonathan Pingle called the meeting a 'kind of hawkish hold'. He said his call for a January hike could be off because inflation is 'not getting out of control' but is not moving down.

The UST curve steepened after the Fed, with 2s30s 12.7bp steeper and 5s30s 8.6bp steeper, a bull-steepening move. The author notes it could reflect the market questioning the Fed's credibility and its willingness to fight inflation. The move did not continue in overnight trading.

TY 30-day implied vol fell back below 6% to 5.98% after the Fed, from about 6.4% at the start of the week. Call skew has picked up despite Wednesday afternoon flows being heavily tilted to downside structures.
The two largest options trades around the Fed were calls: 18.7k FVZ6 104.50 calls paid 19, and 30k TYZ6 106.50 calls paid 27 (vs 105-31+). Open interest shows the TY calls are new risk.
In SOFR options, the largest flow was a buyer of 30k SFRZ6 95.6875/96.5625 put spreads for 1, which the author reads as new risk from someone positioned for a hawkish outcome or a hike.
The author expects accounts to lean into short front-end vol. Early Thursday flows show accounts selling put spreads to buy call spreads.

No ECB move is expected Thursday. UBS economics expects the press conference to focus on OAT spread widening and potential ECB contingencies, Lagarde's succession plan, and a possible increase in the Minimum Reserve Requirement.

The UK Budget on Wednesday was not well received, but Chancellor Healey avoided upsetting the Gilt market. Difficult decisions were deferred, and talk of an earlier election or another fiscal event in the spring continues.
Healey said on the BBC that 'the system is unsustainable' and that the benefits bill will be reduced. The OBR said welfare spending will rise by about £16bn a year until 2031/32.

The OBR's Economic and Fiscal Outlook (section 3.46) warns that changes to property income taxes risk 'a steady long-term rise in rents if demand outstrips supply', which it considers more likely than not.

Markets still price just over 100bp of Bank of England hikes by July 2027, unchanged despite comments from Chief Economist Huw Pill. The author says fiscal policy is not helping the BoE, and an early election is a speculative risk to the expected rate path.
Gulf newsflow has increased. The WSJ reports that VP JD Vance has been engaging Mohsen Rezaei of the Supreme National Security Council to persuade President Trump not to launch fresh attacks.

tension_points.bull_case: The market read the change to the 2027 and 2028 meeting schedule as dovish (fewer live meetings, fewer hikes), and SFRZ7 rallied over 10 ticks. Chair Warsh said the economy was not running too hot and financial conditions were tighter. Some Street commentators say December could be the last hike.
tension_points.bear_case: The author thinks the statement was hawkish, especially with Governor Cook's dissent, and that the dovish inference from fewer meetings is wrong. Markets still price 20.6bp of hikes in December, and Pingle called it a 'kind of hawkish hold'.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Not stated. The author notes the bull-steepening did not continue in overnight trading.
